candidates.text: Bitcoin puked all the way back to $62,000 over the weekend, and a lot of people are asking if they should just sell now before it gets worse. So who's actually dumping here? Is it Binance clawing back billions after the hack? Is it Wall Street raising cash for the Anthropic IPO?

Bitcoin has seen one of its largest liquidation events over the weekend, which has now slapped Bitcoin into a 25 % pullback. And when we ended the show on Friday afternoon, Bitcoin's price was around 70K, was around, sorry, sorry, my guest for the day is messing with my soundboard.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin had a terrible weekend. We went all the way down to 62K, $2 billion in leverage wiped out, $645 million in just 30 minutes. We were just a stone throw away from the 58K gang there, so eat your heart out. And of course, it's putting pressure on everybody. Strategy and metaplan are both making moves while they're down.

More than $1.2 billion in Bitcoin positions were liquidated over the past week with the biggest wave coming on November 12th. So sentiment is about as bad as it can get. But let's see what traders are actually doing with their money. So, Sean, with the mood this dark, where are you seeing traders positioned across the exchanges right now?

With Bitcoin still near its lowest level since July, a strong dollar and more Fed hikes on the table. How are the big asset managers playing this market? We turn now to a familiar face here on the show. Joining us now is Blue Machilari, head of digital asset strategy at T -Rowe Price.

Billions of dollars in liquidations, as always, I believe $2 billion on Bitcoin alone just Saturday and Sunday. And further proof that sometimes when market sentiment is generally bad, Bitcoin can really take it on the chin because it's open 24 -7, 365.
Bitcoin below 70K. Buying opportunity or more downside ahead? More downside ahead. This is not the area I like to invest in. Year -end market. Santa Rally or more volatility?
